issues.note: Six protocol revisions are pinned: the SDK's five negotiable legacy revisions (2024-10-07, 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25) reached via the initialize handshake, and 2026-07-28 reached via server/discover plus the per-request _meta envelope. tests/protocol/conformanceMatrix.ts declares one explicit cell per revision x behavior; tests/protocol/conformance.test.ts drives the real createMcpHandler once per pinned cell across ten behaviors (revision negotiation, capability negotiation, undeclared capabilities staying unserved, tool surface, tool schemas, error vocabulary, era-specific result fields, cancellation, JSON-RPC batching, Streamable HTTP transport) = 60 conformant cells. Not-pinned is a third state, never collapsed into either result: resolveCell reaches 'conformant' only from a pinned declaration whose fixture ran AND passed, a pinned cell with no executing fixture resolves to 'unproven' and fails the gate, and MCP Tasks / MCP Apps are declared not_pinned with reasons rather than omitted. scripts/conformance-matrix.ts is the gate — it binds vitest results back to cells via the [conformance <revision> <behavior>] token and fails on an unproven cell, a failing cell, an orphan fixture, a failed check bound to no cell (how revision drift surfaces), or a stale docs/PROTOCOL_CONFORMANCE.md. All four failure modes were exercised live before landing. CI runs the gate as a named step in .github/workflows/ci.yml. The published matrix names revisions and behaviors and quotes no coverage percentage, and keeps supported / merged / conformance-proven apart.

issues.note: src/lib/runnerEligibility.ts judges seven capability dimensions (runtime location, credential custody, network exposure, lifecycle control, cancellation, audit trail, approval enforcement) against a declared posture, as a strict attended < unattended < public ratchet. Absent evidence and negative evidence never share a code path: no record scores unproven -> needs_evidence, a negative record scores refuted -> ineligible. An attestation without a source counts in neither direction; a malformed record is absence, never a refusal. Fails closed — no/empty/malformed profile returns needs_evidence, and no input yields eligible without a positive sourced record for every required dimension. Reachability is recorded but is deliberately not an input to the decision. export_build_brief takes runner_posture (default 'public'), runner_reachable, and runner_capability_profile, and exports the decision plus per-dimension evidence as the runner_eligibility field and in §9 for runner-hostable targets only. Presence/absence fixture pairs cover every required dimension at every posture. Compact-response size ceiling raised 90 KB -> 96 KB deliberately: the canonical compact response was already at 98.3% of the old budget, so the evidence could not fit under it.

issues.note: Found by LAB's promotion-queue session (/promote, orchestratelab PR #58) by doing it and reverting: promoting a playbook past its still-candidate golden-path route made loadRegistry({ includeBeta: true }) throw 'Unknown route id' for EVERY caller (not just the one playbook), and validate_playbook_candidate read playbooks only — nothing in the MCP could certify a route at all. Fixed both halves, the atomic-pair option (not 'route inherits playbook certification'), since it is the one that keeps loadRegistry structurally unbreakable by a half-promotion. (1) src/registry/registryValidation.ts + registryAssembly.ts: validateCrossReferences resolves golden_path_route_id against the full unfiltered route set first; a route that exists but is invisible only at the current status filter is now a severity:'warning' entry that never fails a strict load (a genuinely unknown route id is still a hard error). (2) A new CI/lint gate, lintPlaybookRouteStatusOrder in registryLint.ts, makes the drift impossible to land in the first place. It deliberately does NOT use a raw status-rank comparison: src/registry/lifecycleStatus.ts's routeLagsBehindPlaybook models the real constraint that beta/candidate are gated behind two INDEPENDENT loadRegistry flags (includeBeta, includeCandidates) while published/validated need neither — a naive rank check was caught live wrongly flagging 7 real 'published' playbooks pointing at merely-'validated' routes (both load with zero flags, always fine) before it shipped. (3) validate_playbook_candidate gained an optional route_yaml input: supplying it certifies the playbook + route pair together, reporting pair_qualifies_for as the lower of each side's own structural DoD ceiling, and pair_status_mismatch:true with a plain blocking sentence — never a throw — when the playbook's declared status is already ahead of its route's. Locked by tests/registry/registryLoader.test.ts (drives the exact LAB failure plus a regression guard for a truly-unknown route id), tests/registry/registryLint.test.ts (the new gate, including the published/validated non-violation case), and 7 new cases in tests/tools/validatePlaybookCandidate.test.ts. pnpm verify: 2358/2358.
Explicit invoice-payment instructions now deterministically require human approval without fuzzy-matching ordinary phrases such as pay attention.

Goal-constraint phrase tables were matched with bare String.includes, so a phrase sitting inside a longer word counted as if the user had written it. 'posts the result in the same THREAD ONLY after I approve' contains 'read only' (th-read only) and fired the read-only prohibition on a goal that explicitly asks the agent to POST, degrading constraint_label to gaps; 'unread only', 'spread only', 'thread-only', 'no written approval' and 'preview before' (vs the approval phrase 'review before') failed the same way. Matching is now whole-word via (?<!\w)...(?!\w) lookarounds in src/lib/constraintSignals.ts, shared by constraintCoverage's own firstMatch. Inflections that substring matching had covered implicitly are now ENUMERATED in the tables (never writes, never edits/editing, never commits/committing) so a reader can see exactly what fires. The chat_triggered_assistant golden fixture's coverage_tags: ['read_only'] was a mislabel produced by this bug and is corrected.
